cells.remarks: States that the image of Dakshiṇamūrti was installed by Karikālaśōla-Settiydr the agent of the compat of Pāyāyar of Karanigai and a gift of land at Tirukkottaram-uḍaiyānādu, in Tenkaviri-nāḍu a sub-division of Rājarāja-vālanādu, etc. Registers an agreement made by the Adhipanāsyam, Maṇi- grāmam, Sāmanta-pōdäli and others reading in the village, prosecuting to levy certain taxes for the expenses of the temple and enjoining that whatever may be the cost of rebuilding in stone the ruined mandapa in front of the temple of god Sarvātthabham-uḍaiya-Nāyanar, which had been commenced by Vaḍugalvar, the daughter-in-law of Śivālayattil-uḍaiya-nāchchiyār and the daughter of Viśvālayattil-nāchchiyār, it shall be met from the tirttam- uḍaiya-nayanar at Tittānāpu m-Muttugram.

cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Kōpīśvarasvāmin temple.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant by Periyayandān, son of Alasani …….. (?) (conditional free of several pieces of land at Kōnātam to the temple of Sakuchathia-Linga. The village Kōkaim di in the Ghangikōdu-sīma was granted by the king as sravamārya to the donor. The grant was free on the river-side in the village of Bucha-palli on the occasion of a solar eclipse. The inscription is followed by another which says that Mammandāju, the son of Katla Mummandāju Tippana and the athala-kiramam of Kōkatam reconsocrated the god Sakalēśvaradēva in this temple.

cells.place: On the four faces of a stone called 'Vinayaka-maḍam' on the bund of the big tank in the same village.
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Poomēvula etc., States that as Nambi Saṅkaran-Vāsudēvar of Tiruvēdiwa-lam, the agent of the (Travancore king) Ravi-Kodaivar-man alias Vijayarāgarāya, had repaired the bund of the big tank of the Maṇakāmaṇi-maḍam, which had breached owing to heavy rains in the month Māsi, they vand-oulled respectively Vāsudēvap-peruṅgarai and Vāsu-dēvap-poravai. A gift of land was also made by Nambi-Saṅkaran for keeping the bund in repair.

cells.place: Nagarjunikoṇḍa (near Puḷḷareḍḍigudem).—On five pieces of a pillar excavated on the east side of the mound called the 'Oṭtaguṇṭa'.
cells.remarks: Portions lost. Seems to record the gift of this pillar of the Mahachaitya enshrining the relics of the Buddha by Bodhisiri, daughter of Vasiṣhṭhiputra Siri- Chantamula, who was the wife of (the latter's) Sēnāpati, the Mahātalavara Vāsiṣhṭhiputra Kandasiri of the Pōkiya clan. Chatamula is said to have 'performed the horse- sacrifice of Khandasagaramanka'.

cells.place: On a slab set up in a plain called Barābahaḍikallaguḍde in the same hamlet (on the west side of the road to Uḍupi).
cells.remarks: Records that when Balamina-Vodeya was governing the provinces Bārkūru-rājya, Nanna, Panna and other citizens of Bārkūru-rājya, gave a piece of land in Barābahaḍikallaguḍde, (specified), to Śrī Narasiṁha-Bhārati-Vodeya of Śrigeri. Also states that certain lands were granted to the same personage for the worship of the Kapila god Kōteśvara, and the worship of the god Viṣhṇu of Baḷukku, by Baḷukkuṇṇayurya, the king's capital, and made some gifts of gold etc. in the presence of the ministers and grand-fathers (of the king), Manasāgōpa a brother-pauji (of the king). Damaged. Seema to register a grant. Built in at the bottom. Damaged. Seema to register a grant of land for the regular worship of the god Kōteśvara.
